summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling strategy. Reviewed pilot telemetry, workload burst patterns, tail latency targets, and trade-offs between warm pool sizing vs. burst capacity. Agreed on data handoff for a live perf run and to iterate autoscale thresholds. Action items assigned.
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-26 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~50m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (BrightBridge CTO), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), Roberto Santos (SRE), Maya Thompson (Product)

00:00 - Sophie: hey everybody, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda: run through the latest pilot metrics, talk autoscale and burst plans for Dedicated, identify risk areas, and agree next steps.
00:09 - Dr. Elena: yep that's perfect, we mostly want to make sure spikes from periodic claims processing won't throttle our front-end.
00:15 - Marcus: great, i'll start with the telemetry we looked at — last week's test window, 8/19 to 8/25. we got a 24-hour rolling view and some hourly histograms.
00:28 - Marcus: overall qps peaked at ~220 rps for short bursts, sustained baseline around 35 rps. interestingly, the 99th percentile token latency jumped during bursts to ~460ms, and tail was 700-900ms in the worst minute. some of that is cold-start influence.
00:47 - Roberto: just to confirm, those numbers are from your hosted env or Dedicated pilot?
00:52 - Marcus: these are running on the Dedicated pilot pool you provisioned last week — 4xA100-equivalent nodes, quantized model v1.2 with prefix caching enabled.
01:05 - Sophie: also worth noting our prefix cache hit rate is ~62% during normal traffic but drops to ~28% during the big ingest windows — that's contributing to the latency rise.
01:18 - Priya: ok that makes sense; the claims flow sends longer prompts in the burst windows. we can share the trace to show token distribution.
01:25 - Diego: quick thought — two knobs to tune: increase warm-pool size to reduce cold starts vs allow larger burst headroom with queueing and graceful degradation. warm pool is costlier but reduces tail latency.
01:40 - Maya: do you have a ballpark cost delta? warm pool vs burst credits?
01:44 - Sophie: rough math — doubling warm pool capacity from 4 to 8 nodes increases steady monthly cost by ~1.9x for that pool; burst credits/overprovisioning that we offer is metered, so you pay more only when you actually burst. for your observed burst profile, a modest warm pool plus a small burst buffer looked like the best tradeoff.
02:03 - Dr. Elena: what's the behavior when the burst buffer is exhausted? do requests get queued or fail?
02:09 - Marcus: we have a tiered fallback. primary: scale up to burst nodes (if credits left). secondary: queue requests with configurable timeout and priority; tertiary: fallback to a lighter-weight model variant (lower token length/quantized) or return degraded responses with a flag. we can tune the queue timeout and the fallbacks per route.
02:31 - Rob: our SLO is 95th < 200ms and 99th < 400ms for sync endpoints — those burst figures are worrying.
02:38 - Sophie: noted. for sync endpoints we recommend stricter warm pool or pre-warming before planned scheduled jobs. for unpredictable spikes we rely on autoscale + burst credits but agree the tail will be higher.
02:49 - Priya: we also need to consider cold-starts from model variant loading — we saw a 2-3s penalty occasionally when the kv cache was flushed.
02:58 - Marcus: yes, kv cache eviction during node churn is critical. we recommend sticky routing for short TTL to maintain cache locality during bursts.
03:10 - Speaker 3: (mumble) have you tried pinning a smaller quantized variant for fast path?
03:16 - Diego: yes we tested q4_0 and q2_K variants; the smaller quantized model reduces latency 20-30% at cost of a ~2-3% quality delta on our eval prompts. might be acceptable for lower-priority traffic.
03:32 - Maya: how would we route lower-priority traffic automatically?
03:35 - Marcus: per-route policies. you can mark endpoints as 'latency-sensitive' or 'best-effort'. requests labeled best-effort get routed to quantized variants during load. we attach a header or token metadata to control that.
03:48 - Dr. Elena: important for compliance — do audit logs show which model variant responded? we need that for our QA team.
03:55 - Sophie: yes, every response includes model_id metadata and there's an audit trail in the Console; we also provide retention and export options (S3, SIEM).
04:07 - Priya: thanks. quick question on network: we're in Azure, is there any cross-region fallback complexity? our main region is east-us-2 and some bursts originate from app instances in west-eu.
04:19 - Marcus: smart routing supports region policies — can route by latency or cost. cross-region fallback will add network latency; for strict SLOs we prefer local regional Dedicated pools or an ingress proxy to reduce egress.
04:33 - Roberto: can you show an example autoscale policy we could apply?
04:36 - Marcus: sure — high-level: min_capacity: 4 nodes, warm_pool: 2 nodes, scale_up_threshold: 70% GPU util over 30s window, scale_down_threshold: 25% over 120s window, max_burst_nodes: 6, burst_credit_limit: X credits per 24h, queue_timeout: 2s default, fallback_model: q2_K. I'll attach a concrete JSON after the call.
04:58 - Dr. Elena: the queue_timeout of 2s is pretty tight for our UX. we might prefer some in-flight degraded responses rather than long waits.
05:05 - Sophie: we can set a route-level policy so your real-time UI uses no-queue and warm pool only, while batch processing endpoints accept queueing and fallback.
05:14 - Priya: what's the expected scale-up time? booting an extra node + model load — is that seconds or minutes?
05:19 - Diego: depends on model size and quantization. for your quantized v1.2 with warm cache, node attach ~20-40s; model load might add 30-90s if cache cold. warm pool reduces that. the burst credits allow immediate short-term capacity while the new nodes finish loading.
05:38 - Roberto: that's still potentially a minute of elevated latency. how do we benchmark that?
05:42 - Marcus: proposed test: a 2-hour perf run, start at baseline 40 rps, inject synthetic bursts to 250 rps for 10-minute windows, repeat 4x. measure 50/95/99/99.9 token latencies, cache hit rate, and cost delta. we'll run it on the Dedicated pilot with both warm_pool and burst-only configs to compare.
06:00 - Dr. Elena: ok, schedule it. we'll give you a maintenance window 2025-09-08 02:00-06:00 UTC.
06:08 - Sophie: noted — we'll put that on the calendar after we get your 7-day trace.
06:12 - Maya: any security considerations for allowing Redwood to spin up extra nodes in our VPC? we need to keep keys managed by our KMS.
06:19 - Sophie: for Dedicated Private mode you can provision nodes inside your VPC with customer-managed KMS; for the current pilot (hosted Dedicated) we can provide envelope encryption and a KMS integration — keys are customer-managed if you want. audit logs and SSO are supported.
06:33 - Priya: great. one more thing — for compliance we need to ensure model caching doesn't persist PHI beyond request scope. is cache scoped per-tenant and TTL-controlled?
06:43 - Marcus: yes, cache entries are tenant-scoped and TTL is configurable; for PHI-sensitive routes we recommend disabled persistent caching and instead use short-lived in-memory caches that are flushed after request. We'll document the knob.
06:55 - Dr. Elena: perfect. back to sizing: are there rules of thumb for warm pool sizing given burst magnitude and frequency?
07:03 - Marcus: rule of thumb: warm_pool >= expected 95th percentile sustained concurrent model contexts; if bursts are rare and short, rely more on burst credits. also consider model loading time: if model load > 60s, warm pool is advisable. For you, with 10-min bursts and ~250 rps peaks, warm_pool of 4-6 and max_burst 6 seems reasonable.
07:25 - Sophie: operationally we recommend a hybrid: base=4 nodes, warm_pool=4, max_burst=6 with burst credits cap, and route-specific fallbacks. that gives you steady low tail for sync endpoints and headroom for batch.
07:39 - Roberto: let's talk about cost transparency — we want token-level cost breakdown and per-route cost attribution in the Console.
07:46 - Diego: Console already supports token-level and per-route breakdowns; we can share a dashboard with your team and hook to your billing export.
07:53 - Priya: good. can we simulate cost for projected 3-month usage?
07:57 - Sophie: yes, we'll include that in the SOW. we'll base it on the 7-day trace and the two configs (warm pool heavy vs burst-heavy).
08:06 - Maya: any gotchas on model quantization compatibility with our accuracy requirements? the legal team will want to know QA impact.
08:14 - Marcus: quantization test matrix we've run shows minimal regression on our eval; we'll run your eval set too. quality regressions are surfaced in Redwood Optimize with per-prompt diffs so you can gate.
08:27 - Dr. Elena: excellent. question — can we limit which team members can change autoscale policies via RBAC?
08:33 - Sophie: yes, RBAC is role-based and audit-logged. we can set edit permissions to a small admin group.
08:39 - Speaker 1: (crosstalk) how about emergency throttle controls?
08:43 - Marcus: operators can trigger manual capacity caps or flip a kill-switch to route to a safe-model. we also support programmatic webhooks for automated runbooks.
08:54 - Sophie: i just pushed the deck link in chat (link to shared drive).
08:58 - Priya: got it. i see the autoscale JSON sample.
09:02 - Marcus: i'll go deeper into the autoscale playbook — want to call out specific alerts: sustained GPU util > 80% for 45s = scale up alert; scale-down protected window 5m post-scale-up to avoid flapping; burst-credit threshold 15% of daily budget triggers backpressure.
09:22 - Dr. Elena: can we get those alerts into PagerDuty?
09:26 - Sophie: yes, integrations exist for PagerDuty, Slack, and Datadog.
09:30 - Roberto: log retention — we need 1 year for audit. can you support that?
09:34 - Diego: yes, longer retention is an add-on. we can export logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
09:40 - Maya: any recommended experiments before the perf run? maybe a smaller-scale warm pool test?
09:45 - Marcus: recommend two pre-tests: 1) 1-hour warm-pool-only run to validate 95/99 under sustained 80 rps; 2) short 30min burst-only with aggressive burst to validate fallback behavior. then full perf run.
09:58 - Priya: we'll try to free up infra for those windows.
10:02 - Sophie: ok let's recap next steps. Sophie to send SOW and cost models; Marcus to send autoscale playbook + JSON; BrightBridge to provide 7-day trace; schedule perf run for 2025-09-08; action items in chat.
10:18 - Dr. Elena: sounds good. thanks team.
10:22 - Sophie: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and update the calendar.
10:27 - End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words preserved; some technical acronyms transcribed phonetically (e.g., q2_K as q2 underscore k, KV cache sometimes appears as keevy cache in raw audio).
